correctness.rationale: The initial opposite part-majority process reduces exactly to a first-appearance random permutation, giving the hypergeometric conditional probability. Alignment is absorbing at the level of part majorities and yields almost sure unanimity. Independent binomial weighting yields the finite formula. Exponential-clock order-statistic means and variance justify normalized-margin comparison at CLT scale; Cauchy normal-ratio wedge gives the asserted finite-ratio arcsine limit. A separate exact absorbing-Markov-recurrence implementation agreed on 784 conditional cases and brute initial-profile enumeration agreed on three graphs. Finite computations support, but do not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The result measures the probability that local social learning overrides the initial population-wide majority in a natural two-community network. The hypergeometric probability gives a complete exact finite law, and the nontrivial explicit arcsine curve resolves the dependence on relative community size. This identifies a meaningful structural phenomenon rather than an arbitrary finite parameter count.
